query: Executive Order 14409 'Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security' signed June 2, 2026: what does it require, what deadlines does it set for CAISI/NIST and other agencies, and what implementation milestones fall in July-September 2026? Have OpenAI and Anthropic signed agreements under it?
answer:
Research complete. Summary of what matters most for the forecast:

**The framing correction that changes the analysis:** CAISI is not named in EO 14409. The order's frontier-model work goes to Treasury / NSA / CISA, with NIST merely consulted and the NSA Director holding sole designation authority. Reporting says NSA *and* CAISI will jointly conduct reviews, but that's press sourcing, not the text.

**On the direct question — no.** Neither OpenAI nor Anthropic has signed a publicly announced agreement under EO 14409. Multiple outlets state flatly that no agreements were announced after the Aug 4 ONCD briefing. What exists is endorsement (Altman: the order "gets the balance right"), joint editing of the draft, and one unilateral Anthropic commitment to the Gold Eagle clearinghouse.

**Three facts that pull in opposite directions for the Aug 10 – Sept 3 window:**

1. The event class already fired recently — CAISI's **May 5, 2026** announcement renegotiated *both* the OpenAI and Anthropic MOUs while adding Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and xAI. That is precisely the described event, ~3 months before the window.
2. The agency that would announce it has been muzzled — National Cyber Director Cairncross directed CAISI to stop publishing model assessments while the EO is implemented (WSJ). Internal testing continues; the public channel is off.
3. Something is genuinely brewing but undated — WIRED (Aug 12) reports a "more robust arrangement" under discussion that "could eventually result in labs becoming formal partners in testing programs," on a "coming months" horizon.

**Dated items inside the window:** the Senate Democrats' requested response deadline (~Sept 2) and the FAI FOIA clock (early September). Both are transparency-forcing, not agreement announcements. Nothing else is scheduled.

The administration's disclosure posture across this entire period has been secrecy by design — classified benchmarks, an unpublished framework, an explicit refusal to announce agreements post-meeting, and a suspended public evaluation channel.

One caveat I'd flag: an aggregator (neomanex.com) claims the Aug 1 deadline lapsed with zero deliverables. Axios, CNBC, Fortune, WIRED, and Reuters all contradict this. I treated it as an outlier and recorded it as such rather than dropping it.

sources.snippet: Sec. 3. Secure Frontier Model Deployment. Within 60 days of the date of this order, the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of War, through the Director of NSA, and the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Director of CISA... shall: (a) develop and maintain a classified benchmarking process... (b) design a voluntary framework with AI developers...

sources.title: White House to host AI companies to review new model-testing framework

Instead, the details will be kept under wraps, only known to a select group of companies that may choose to participate in the process, which is voluntary.

sources.snippet: WASHINGTON, Aug 4 (Reuters) - The Trump administration told AI developers on Tuesday that it will not put open-weight AI models through voluntary safety tests, according to two sources familiar with the discussions.

sources.title: The White House Is Keeping Its AI Cybersecurity Framework Secret
sources.snippet: The Trump administration has finalized a plan to address the cybersecurity risks posed by increasingly capable artificial intelligence models, a White House official confirmed to WIRED. But at least for now, it's deliberately keeping the details under wraps.

sources.title: The White House Is Going to Expand Its AI Policy
sources.snippet: White House officials are almost certain to revise the Trump administration's new artificial intelligence guidelines and expand its oversight of AI models. A White House official says the framework is expected to cover open models too 'in the coming months.' The White House is under pressure to draft a 'more robust arrangement' with leading AI labs, which could eventually result in labs becoming formal partners in testing programs.

sources.title: Trump administration's closed-door AI framework catches tech policy sector off guard
sources.snippet: Representatives from Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI and Microsoft attended last week's briefing, according to the sources, while Forbes reported staff from Nvidia and smaller companies attended. The Foundation for American Innovation filed a Freedom of Information Act request to the White House's Office of the National Cyber Director for the release of the framework.

sources.title: White House Intros Classified Cybersecurity Review for Frontier AI Models
sources.snippet: Representatives from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Nvidia and other leading AI companies recently met with administration officials to discuss the framework. The White House did not announce any agreements following the meeting or publicly disclose how models will be evaluated before their broader release.

sources.title: White House Advances Secretive Cybersecurity Review for Frontier AI Models
sources.snippet: No participant has publicly described a final agreement from Tuesday's meeting. Sens. Kirsten Gillibrand, Adam Schiff, Mark Warner, Christopher Coons, and Mark Kelly called for a public, technically grounded framework and requested an unclassified response, with a classified annex if necessary, within 30 days.

sources.title: White House Frontier AI Cybersecurity Framework Takes Shape, but Key Details Stay Secret
sources.snippet: Staffers from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Nvidia, and other AI companies were invited to the briefing. No official announcement followed the meeting, and the details of the framework remain confidential.

sources.title: As AI models break free, White House works with firms on secret safety measures
sources.snippet: Companies that agree to the framework will submit their models to U.S. inspectors to be evaluated for safety for 30 days before those companies can receive federal funding—including from the Defense Department, whose 2027 budget request seeks more than $54 billion for AI companies.

sources.title: White House AI vetting plan to exempt lower-cost 'open' models
sources.snippet: The White House framework for vetting the cybersecurity risks of advanced artificial intelligence models would focus on the top-tier products from U.S. developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic — while exempting a rising breed of lower-cost AI software.

key_facts: EO 14409 'Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security' was signed June 2, 2026 and published in the Federal Register June 5, 2026 (91 FR 34565, FR Doc 2026-11415, DCPD-202600376).
CAISI is NOT named anywhere in EO 14409. Neither is DOE or ODNI. NIST appears only in a consultative role (Secretary of Commerce through the NIST Director) in Section 3.

Section 3 lead agencies are Treasury, Secretary of War through the NSA Director, and DHS through the CISA Director. Final 'covered frontier model' designation authority rests solely with the Director of NSA.
Section 2 tasks (CNSS, SecWar, DHS/CISA Binding Operational Directives, Treasury AI cybersecurity clearinghouse, OMB grant review) were due within 30 days = July 2, 2026.
Section 3 tasks (classified benchmarking process + voluntary framework) and Section 2(f) (OPM Tech Force expansion) were due within 60 days = August 1, 2026.

Section 3(b) mechanics: developers may engage the government on 'covered frontier model' determination, provide access up to 30 days before release to other trusted partners, and collaborate on selecting trusted partners. An earlier draft floated 90 days; the final version cut it to 30.
Section 3(c) expressly bars any mandatory licensing, preclearance, or permitting requirement; Section 5(c) creates no enforceable right.

NSPM-11, issued June 5, 2026, is a related instrument directing SecDef, Secretary of Energy, DNI, and the NSA Director through the AI Security Center to work with industry on securing data centers and advanced AI technologies — a separate potential vehicle for industry agreements.

July 14, 2026: the 'Gold Eagle' AI cybersecurity clearinghouse was publicly launched, fulfilling Sec. 2(d). Treasury-managed with CISA/DHS/DoW, using a new CMU Software Engineering Institute platform called VINTS. Officials said closed frontier models including Anthropic's Mythos would be used to discover vulnerabilities.

July 27, 2026: The Information reported ONCD circulated a draft framework to OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google roughly two weeks earlier, and the three jointly submitted edits. Same reporting said reviews would be conducted by a combination of NSA and CAISI.

August 3, 2026: The White House stated 'The voluntary framework outlined in the June 2nd executive order is complete. Discussions with industry about next steps are underway.' The framework has not been published.

August 3, 2026: Senators Gillibrand, Schiff, Warner, Coons, and Kelly sent a letter demanding a public, technically grounded framework and an unclassified response (with classified annex if necessary) within 30 days — approximately September 2, 2026.

August 4, 2026: A staff-level, closed-door briefing was held at the Office of the National Cyber Director with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Nvidia plus smaller firms. Reportedly about 30 minutes long.

NO agreements were announced following the August 4 meeting. Multiple outlets state this explicitly: 'The White House did not announce any agreements following the meeting' (Redmondmag Aug 6, Campus Technology Aug 12) and 'No participant has publicly described a final agreement' (Pure AI Aug 5).
As of August 19, 2026, neither OpenAI nor Anthropic has signed a publicly announced agreement under EO 14409.
August 4, 2026: Reuters reported the administration told AI developers it will not put open-weight models through the voluntary safety tests. The framework covers only top-tier closed models.

Nextgov (Aug 7) reported, per two lab officials, that companies agreeing to the framework submit models for 30-day evaluation before those companies can receive federal funding — including from a DoD FY2027 request seeking over $54 billion for AI companies.

OpenAI publicly said within days of the June 2 signing that it would comply and give the government early access; Sam Altman said the order 'gets the balance right.' Anthropic called it 'an important step in strengthening America's leadership in AI.' These are endorsements, not signed agreements.

Anthropic's June 30, 2026 blog post committed to notify government counterparts on jailbreaks/misuse, provide threat intelligence in advance of publication, and participate in the Sec. 2(d) clearinghouse — a unilateral, single-company commitment, not a bilateral Section 3 agreement.

August 2024: The U.S. AI Safety Institute (NIST) signed MOUs with BOTH Anthropic and OpenAI, establishing a framework to receive access to major new models prior to and following public release. AISI was re-established as CAISI in June 2025 by Commerce Secretary Lutnick.
